name: RI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Gabe Amo running with large financial advantage ($1.85M vs $2K)
Polymarket prices Amo at 97% to win
No competitive polling or expert ratings signal vulnerability
model.rationale: This Rhode Island seat leans heavily Democratic, incumbent Gabe Amo is well-funded with $1.85 million on hand against a Republican rival who has raised about $13,000, and prediction markets price his win at 97%. With no polls or ratings suggesting competition, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpectedly strong Republican fundraising could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rhode Island's first district is a solidly Democratic seat, and first-term incumbent Gabe Amo is seeking reelection with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean favors Democrats by double digits, and Amo has built a commanding war chest of roughly $1.85 million while Republican Kellie Keenan has raised only about $13,000 and holds minimal cash. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but lacks visible resources.

No public general-election polling or expert ratings exist for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, and those fundamentals are lopsided. Prediction markets give Amo roughly a 97% chance of winning. The expected outcome is a Democratic victory by a margin in the low twenties, with only modest uncertainty.
